# Copilot / Agent Quick Instructions for Thinkorama

This repository is a small static-site Vue app (no build step). These instructions highlight patterns and decisions an AI coding agent should follow to be immediately productive.

# Key points
- Architecture: static HTML (`index.html`) loads runtime Vue 3 and lightGallery from CDNs. Components are hand-registered as UMD-style objects in `js/` (`gallery.js`, `screensaver.js`, `quickview.js`, `search.js`) and wired by `js/app.js` which mounts the Vue app to `#app`.
- Data flow: `images.json` is the single source of truth for image paths. `images-metadata.json` contains OCR text + AI-generated captions for search. The client fetches both at mount in `js/app.js`. Python scripts regenerate these files from the `images/` folder.
- No build tools: there is no `package.json` or bundler. Edits should preserve plain script includes in `index.html` and avoid assuming ES module imports or npm dependencies.

# Developer workflows (explicit)
- Add images: drop files under `images/` and run locally: `py gen_images_json.py` to update `images.json`.
- Enable AI search: run `source venv/bin/activate && python gen_images_metadata_ai.py` to generate OCR + BLIP-2 captions (requires Tesseract and transformers).
- Run locally: open `index.html` in a browser or serve the folder with a static server (e.g. `python -m http.server 8000`).
- Test LightGallery behavior: ensure CDN versions in `index.html` match the plugins used in `js/*` (the code expects `lightGallery`, `lgZoom`, and `lgThumbnail` globals).

# Project conventions and patterns
- Components: each UI component is a plain object attached to `window` (e.g. `window.gallery`, `window.searchbar`). Keep this pattern when adding components—register on `window` and reference by tag name in `js/app.js`.
- Global constants: `PAGE_SIZE` is declared in `js/app.js` and used by `js/gallery.js`. If changing pagination behavior, update both files.
- Image paths: `images.json` contains relative paths (example: `books/book1.jpg`). Code concatenates `'images/' + path` when building URLs—do not change this format without updating all usages.
- Search: `js/app.js` manages `filteredImages` computed property that filters based on `searchQuery` and `searchFolder`. Gallery displays filtered results while screensaver uses all images.
- Fullscreen / input handling: `screensaver` uses `requestFullscreen()` and `keydown` listeners; ensure `beforeUnmount` clears intervals and removes listeners.

# What to change and how (examples)
- To add a small feature (example: a download button in lightGallery), update `js/gallery.js` and `index.html` to keep plugin/option parity. Prefer minimal, DOM-focused changes; no bundler-specific code.
- To modify pagination size: change `const PAGE_SIZE = 12;` in `js/app.js` and verify `gallery.totalPages` logic in `js/gallery.js` remains correct.

# Integration and external deps
- External CDNs: `vue@3`, `lightgallery` and its plugins are loaded from CDNs in `index.html`. Code relies on global UMD bundles (no ESM). Any upgrade should be tested in browser—avoid automated upgrades without manual verification.

Files to inspect for context
- `index.html` — script and CSS includes, app mount point.
- `js/app.js` — app entry, `PAGE_SIZE`, data fetching, search state management.
- `js/gallery.js`, `js/quickview.js`, `js/screensaver.js`, `js/search.js` — component implementations and runtime assumptions.
- `gen_images_json.py` and `images.json` — image paths generation workflow.
- `gen_images_metadata.py` and `images-metadata.json` — OCR text extraction for search.
- `requirements.txt` — Python dependencies (pytesseract, Pillow).

# Behavior constraints to preserve
- Keep the runtime global-registration pattern for components.
- Preserve `images.json` as array of relative paths and the `'images/' + path` concatenation.
- `images-metadata.json` structure: array of objects with `{path, text, folder, filename}`.
- Search is client-side only (filtering in Vue computed property), no backend API.
- Components expect browser globals (no SSR). Avoid adding server-side code unless adding a new service and documenting it.

# OCR Search Feature
- Uses Tesseract OCR to extract text from images during build/setup phase
- `gen_images_metadata.py` processes all images and creates `images-metadata.json`
- Search component (`js/search.js`) provides text search and category filtering
- Filtering happens client-side in `js/app.js` via `filteredImages` computed property
- Search works on: extracted OCR text, filenames, and folder names
- Optional: if `images-metadata.json` doesn't exist, search UI won't appear (graceful degradation)
